name: Pale Greyish Violet-Blue
lede: Pale Greyish Violet-Blue is a soft periwinkle, built by putting the modifiers pale and greyish in front of the base color [[violet-blue]].

sections.title: Two modifiers on violet-blue
sections.body:
Pale Greyish Violet-Blue stacks two modifier words, pale and greyish, in front of the base color [[violet-blue]], in the compound-modifier grammar our library uses for names like this one [1]. Robert Ridgway first listed this swatch in his 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature*, plate XXIV, hue 53, tone d, and the Inter-Society Color Council later filed it in the ISCC-NBS 1955 system as block 199 (R) [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[wild-blue-yonder]], 2.6 units off, a touch duller [2]; [[chicory-blue]] sits 3.4 units away, and [[pale-soft-blue-violet]] 3.6 units away, slightly more vivid and purpler [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a color within range of this swatch in 63 of 23,781 paintings, 0.26 percent, as photographed; looking for real coverage inside each painting narrows that to 40, rarer than 53 percent of the named colors in our library [3]. It most often plays an accent, in 32 percent of its 40 appearances by lightness rank, so varnish cannot fake the result [3].

The earliest match dates to 1474, Piero della Francesca's year, 438 years before Ridgway's 1912 plate, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin; it marks a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a surviving pigment or dye [3].
